official.deadline_note: Earlier rounds: Early Decision I and Early Action due 1 November 2026 (decisions 1 and 15 December; deposits 15 January and 1 May); Early Decision II and Regular Decision due 1 February 2027 (decisions 1 and 15 March; deposits 15 March and 1 May). All financial aid materials must be submitted by the deadline of the chosen admissions round and incomplete applications are not reviewed. Early Decision is binding; Early Action and Regular Decision are nonbinding.
official.application_cycle: Current first-year admissions cycle: Early Decision I and Early Action 1 November 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision 1 February 2027, with financial aid materials due by the round's deadline.
official.status_note: Trinity publishes the current first-year decision plans: Early Decision I and Early Action applications due 1 November with decisions in December, Early Decision II and Regular Decision due 1 February with decisions in March. There is no fee for applications submitted online, the CSS Profile opens 1 October, and all aid materials are tied to the chosen round's deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Trinity's 2026-27 undergraduate Cost of Attendance lists tuition and fees of $59,280 with a total cost of attendance of $77,846 residing on campus; institutional need-based aid is determined against that cost of attendance, and the EducationUSA listing for this programme states need-based financial aid is awarded up to the cost of attendance.
benefits: International students are automatically considered for academic merit scholarships ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 per year.
Historically, scholarships have ranged from $5,000 to $35,000 USD per year and are renewable for four years, or eight semesters.
Trinity does not offer loans to international students. All scholarships and financial aid for international students are grants - funds you don't have to repay.
All international students are eligible for Trinity on-campus employment, regardless of financial need.
There is no fee for applications submitted online, and scholarships are awarded automatically at the time of admission with no separate scholarship application.
eligibility: If you are not a U.S. citizen or U.S. permanent resident, you should apply to Trinity as an international student, regardless of where you attended secondary school.
All international applicants are considered for general merit-based scholarships based on the materials submitted with their application for admission.
International transfer students are not eligible for financial aid from Trinity; Trinity does not accept transfer applications from international students who require financial aid.
Trinity requires proof of English language proficiency for all international applicants (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo), with waivers for qualifying English-instruction backgrounds.

International applicants should typically complete 4 years of literature/writing/grammar, 3 years of college preparatory mathematics including algebra II and trigonometry, precalculus, or statistics, 3 years of science including at least 2 laboratory sciences, 3 years of social science, and 2 years of the same foreign language.
requirements: All applicants must complete the Statement of Financial Responsibility form in their Trinity admissions portal; the application cannot be reviewed until this document is complete.
All financial aid materials must be submitted by Trinity's published application deadlines; incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

To be considered for need-based financial aid, students must submit the CSS Profile for International Students or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application with their application for admission.

All secondary school records must be submitted in English, with certified English translations if not originally in English, and must be sent by a school counselor or school official - student-submitted records are not accepted.
Acceptable English proficiency tests are TOEFL, IELTS, and the Duolingo English Test; Trinity does not accept superscoring, and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted.
Need-based grant renewal is based on continued demonstrated financial need, available funding, and satisfactory academic progress.
documents: Completed online application (Common Application or Coalition Application for international applicants; ApplyTexas is also listed among accepted platforms) with personal essay
Official secondary school records or transcripts in English, submitted by a school counselor or school official
English proficiency test scores (TOEFL or IELTS self-reported in the Trinity portal; Duolingo results sent directly by the testing service)
Secondary School Report with a counselor or school-head letter of recommendation, and a Teacher Evaluation Form with a letter from a core academic subject instructor
Statement of Financial Responsibility / International Student Financial Aid Agreement completed in the Trinity admissions portal
For need-based aid only: CSS Profile for International Students submitted through College Board (Trinity code 6831) or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application
Bank statements and certifications of financing, required of enrolling students before the I-20 or DS-2019 can be issued
selection_criteria: Merit scholarships are based on the strength of the academic profile: the rigor of and performance in secondary school coursework, standardized test scores, the strength of the essay, involvement outside the classroom, and recommendations from school officials.

Trinity reviews international applications holistically, considering the academic record, coursework rigor, writing, extracurricular involvement, and recommendations in the context of the applicant's educational environment.
Trinity is need-aware in its review of international applications; applicants who can contribute at least $45,000 USD per year toward educational expenses are the most competitive for admission.
Interviews submitted through platforms such as InitialView and Vericant are considered but are not required.
Grant funds are limited and awarded based on eligibility and availability; early application is recommended.
coverage: Merit scholarships historically range from $5,000 to $35,000 USD per year, renewable for four years or eight semesters.

Need-based financial aid is applied for through Trinity's admissions process; the EducationUSA listing for this programme states aid is awarded up to the cost of attendance (2026-27 cost of attendance on trinity.edu: $77,846 residing on campus).
All scholarships and financial aid for international students are grants - funds you don't have to repay; Trinity does not offer loans to international students.
On-campus employment is available to all international students regardless of financial need; a job is not guaranteed and payment is based on hours worked.
No athletic scholarships are offered - Trinity is an NCAA Division III school, though student athletes remain eligible for merit and need-based aid through the admission application.

Have a school counselor or official submit official secondary school records in English, the Secondary School Report, and a recommendation.
Have a core academic subject instructor submit the Teacher Evaluation Form and a letter of recommendation.
Submit English proficiency scores (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo) or request a waiver in the Trinity application portal.
Complete the Statement of Financial Responsibility / International Student Financial Aid Agreement in the Trinity admissions portal - required of every applicant.
If seeking need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile for International Students (code 6831) or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application by the same round deadline.
Track status in the applicant portal; at enrollment, provide bank statements and certifications of financing for I-20/DS-2019 issuance.
official.application_route: One online application (Common Application, Coalition, or ApplyTexas) by the chosen decision-plan deadline; merit consideration is automatic, while need-based aid requires the CSS Profile or Trinity's in-portal International Student Financial Aid Application plus the mandatory Statement of Financial Responsibility.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are not U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents; such applicants apply as international students regardless of where they attended secondary school.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarships and financial aid are exclusively for international (non-U.S. citizen / non-U.S. permanent resident) first-year applicants.
official.duration: Merit scholarships are renewable for four years, or eight semesters; need-based grants must be renewed annually based on continued demonstrated need, available funding, and satisfactory academic progress (continuing-student priority filing deadline 1 March).
official.description: Trinity University awards international first-year applicants automatic merit scholarships historically ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 per year and renewable for four years, alongside limited, competitive need-based grant aid reviewed through a need-aware admissions process. All financial aid for international students is grant aid - Trinity does not offer loans - and every international student is also eligible for on-campus employment.
official.region: North America - San Antonio, Texas, USA
official.program_type: University-awarded merit scholarships plus competitive need-based grant aid for international first-year undergraduates; no separate scholarship application.
official.english_requirement: Proof of English proficiency is required for all international applicants via TOEFL, IELTS, or the Duolingo English Test; published recommended scores are TOEFL 5.5, IELTS 7.0, and Duolingo 130. No superscoring is accepted and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted. Waivers are available if English is the applicant's first language and the primary language of the home or home country, or if English was the language of instruction for the final four consecutive years of secondary school (students in English language support courses during those four years are not eligible).

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you apply for separately: every international first-year file at Trinity is automatically scored for merit grants of $5,000-$35,000 a year, and the single Statement of Financial Responsibility in the admissions portal gates the entire review. Because Trinity reads international files need-aware, the aid ask and the admission decision are effectively one decision, so a family that can document roughly $45,000 a year is applying from a far stronger position. Against 2026-27 tuition and fees of $59,280 and a total cost of attendance of $77,846, even a top merit grant leaves a real balance, and Trinity will not lend to international students.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-U.S. high-school students whose families can fund most of a roughly $78,000-a-year budget and who want renewable merit grants without a separate scholarship essay or interview.
application_readiness_checklist: File the Common or Coalition application early enough that school documents and the portal Statement of Financial Responsibility clear well before your round's deadline - Trinity states the file cannot be reviewed without that form.
Ask your counselor to send transcripts from their official school email with certified English translations; student-uploaded records are not accepted.
Decide merit-only versus need-based before you apply, because adding the CSS Profile moves you into Trinity's most competitive applicant pool and delays the admission decision.
Budget for the CSS Profile (Trinity offers no fee waivers) or plan to complete Trinity's free in-portal International Student Financial Aid Application entirely in English and USD.
If relying on an English-test waiver, confirm English was the language of instruction for your final four consecutive secondary years and that you took no English-support courses in that period.
Line up bank statements and certification of financing early; enrolling students cannot receive the I-20 or DS-2019 without them.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the Statement of Financial Responsibility - Trinity states the application cannot be reviewed until it is complete.
Transcripts uploaded by the student instead of sent by a counselor or school official from a school email address.
CSS Profile evidence submitted as screenshots - only the official College Board report under code 6831 is accepted.
Requesting need-based aid with a family contribution far below roughly $45,000 a year, which need-aware review turns into a much harder admission bet.
Aid materials arriving after the chosen round's deadline; incomplete files are not reviewed and the admission decision is withheld until the aid application arrives.
International transfer applicants assuming they can receive aid - Trinity offers none to international transfers.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: With 2026-27 tuition and fees of $59,280 and a total cost of attendance of $77,846 residing on campus, a top $35,000 merit grant still leaves roughly $43,000 a year for family funds, need-based grants, or on-campus wages, and a $5,000 floor grant leaves about $73,000. Airfare, visa fees, and health insurance sit outside the published cost of attendance entirely.
document_audit: CSS Profile must be submitted officially through College Board with Trinity code 6831 - screenshots are rejected and no fee waiver exists.
Trinity's own International Student Financial Aid Application must be completed entirely in English with every figure converted to USD.
Duolingo scores must be sent directly by the testing service; only TOEFL and IELTS may be self-reported in the applicant portal.
Records not originally in English need certified translations and must still travel through the school, not the applicant.
After admission, bank statements and certifications of financing are prerequisites for the I-20 or DS-2019, so source them during the application cycle, not in August.
alerts: Early Decision is binding while Early Action and Regular Decision are not, and each notification date carries its own deposit deadline (15 January, 1 May, 15 March, 1 May).
Applying for need-based aid means no admission decision until the aid application is received - a timing trap for late filers.
There are no CSS Profile fee waivers, no athletic scholarships (NCAA Division III), and no loans for international students; the funding stack is grants plus campus jobs only.
Merit renewal assumes continued enrollment and progress, and need-based grants reopen annually with a 1 March priority filing date for continuing students.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application per round with school-submitted records and the mandatory portal financial-responsibility form; merit is decided inside the admission review while need-based aid rides on the CSS Profile or the portal aid form filed by the same deadline, with the outcome tracked in the applicant portal.
